description: The operating principles that run throughout the Operations Maturity System. Reference them anywhere a decision, review, or design conversation needs a sharper frame.

principles.text: Design the system before blaming the person.
Ownership must exist at the level where action occurs.
Every metric should support a decision.
Every recurring meeting should have a job.
Scale exposes ambiguity.
Standardize repeatable work, not judgment.
Controls belong where failure becomes expensive.
Decisions should live at the lowest responsible level.
Workarounds are operational signals.
Exceptions reveal process truth.
Complexity must earn its cost.
Visibility without action is reporting theater.
A process without governance will drift.
Capacity is a system constraint, not a motivation problem.
Automation comes after simplification.
Improvement without a baseline is opinion.
Local optimization can damage global performance.
Mature systems make failure visible early.
Operational excellence is designed, not demanded.
The goal is not more process. The goal is more predictable value.
